item.title: Kim Tests Submarine-Launched Missiles After Trump Floats Meeting
item.description: North Korea said it tested submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles, as Pyongyang flexes its military muscle following Donald Trump’s fresh overtures for a meeting with Kim Jong Un.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: White House AI Task Force to Hold First Meeting on Thursday
item.description: The new White House task force on artificial intelligence is expected to hold its first meeting on Thursday, according to two administration officials, as the Trump administration faces mounting pressure to take a more aggressive approach to AI safety.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Money, Markets and the Midterms with Washington Edition
item.description: With control of Congress at stake, money is pouring into the races that could determine the balance of power in Washington. And when Election Day is over, what should policy makers expect? Money, Markets and the Midterms with Washington Edition took Bloomberg.com subscribers inside the strategy, spending and political forces shaping the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore Weighs Legal Action as Haze Turns ‘Very Unhealthy’
item.description: Singapore will “keep its options open” on taking legal action against errant companies as air quality in the city-state deteriorates to very unhealthy levels.
item.dc:creator: Cindy Wang

item.title: Middle East Attacks Increase Uncertainty Over Oil Flow
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mark Esper, former US Defense Secretary, says the US controls the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran can still influence how much traffic moves through it by threatening ships, insurers and crews. Mattie Duppler, Founder and President of Forward Strategies and spokesperson for The Ledger Project, says a rate hike is more likely than not after the latest CPI report came in modestly higher than expected. Rep. Suzan DelBene (D-WA), DCCC Chair, says Republicans are in “triage mode” and moving resources to defend seats they already hold. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China and EU Risk New Trade Clash Over What Comes After Car Deal
item.description: After getting China to accept limits to its car exports, the European Union is already eyeing follow-up action in other industries — setting up their next trade clash.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Hot September CPI Spurs Fed Rate Hike Fears
item.description: US stocks fell on Wednesday, with chipmakers leading declines after stronger than expected consumer price data raised concerns that the Federal Reserve may need to lift interest rates more aggressively than expected in coming months. Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan joins to discuss the bank's latest earnings. MWAG CEO Meredith Whitney examines the state of the US consumer. Mandeep Singh of Bloomberg Intelligence reacts to Anthropic's pre-IPO investor day and the latest comments from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Plus - Allspring's Nate Miles shares the findings from the firm's 2026 retirement study. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Argentina, US Amend Trade Deal in Bid to Secure Ratification
item.description: Argentina and the US agreed on amendments to a trade deal they signed in February, a bid to persuade the South American nation’s legislature to approve the pact.
item.dc:creator: Travis Waldron

item.title: Rep. DelBene Says GOP Spending Shows Defensive Shift
item.description: Rep. Suzan DelBene (D-WA), DCCC Chair, says Republicans are in “triage mode” and moving resources to defend seats they already hold. Rep. DelBene says Democrats are making spending decisions based on race-level data and conditions on the ground as the House map expands. Rep. DelBene says the DCCC is prioritizing frontliners, incumbents and races where it has already invested before adding support to newly competitive contests as more resources come in. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Voters Are Feeling a Deeper Inflation Squeeze: Duppler
item.description: Mattie Duppler, Founder and President of Forward Strategies and spokesperson for The Ledger Project, says a rate hike is more likely than not after the latest CPI report came in modestly higher than expected. Duppler says the data itself matters less politically than how Americans are experiencing higher prices for groceries and gas. Duppler says consumers had a pandemic-era financial cushion when prices rose in 2022, while today they are increasingly using credit cards and savings to cover higher costs. Duppler thinks that financial pressure is what voters will be thinking about as they head to the polls. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Leakers Should Be Shot in Remarks at Arizona Rally
item.description: President Donald Trump called for executing individuals who leak information to the media during a campaign rally as he railed against what he saw as critical coverage of the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Esper Says Iran Can Still Disrupt Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Mark Esper, former US Defense Secretary, says the US controls the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran can still influence how much traffic moves through it by threatening ships, insurers and crews. Esper says Ukraine still has European allies, but pushing back against Russia is harder without full US support, including arms and intelligence. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada Threatens to Force Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) to Sell Assets Over Layoffs
item.description: Canada’s industry minister said the government has the power to force Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. to sell its assets the country, escalating a dispute over job cuts at the company’s steel operations in Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Derek Decloet

item.title: Bolsonaro Holds Narrow Lead Over Lula Ahead of Brazil Runoff
item.description: Right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds a slim lead over President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva less than two weeks before Brazil’s runoff election, a new poll showed.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: US Consumer Prices Rise
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
US consumer prices advanced in September at the fastest pace in five months and a gauge of underlying price pressures rose by more than expected, keeping the squeeze on household budgets ahead of November’s midterm elections. Elsewhere, Bank of America stock and fixed-income traders missed estimates, while Anthropic held a pre-IPO investor day.
On today's episode: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan Mike McKee, Bloomberg News Economics & Policy Correspondent Mandeep Singh, Bloomberg Intelligence Global Head of Tech Research Kelly O. Kay & Jeff Sanders, Partners at Heidrick & Struggles (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How France Got Caught in a Debt Spiral
item.description: Student protests in France are exposing a deeper crisis in the European Union’s second largest economy, which is caught between political anger, mounting debt and nervous bond markets (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Takaichi Trade Gets a Rethink One Year On as Bond Appeal Grows
item.description: For much of Sanae Takaichi’s first year as prime minister, the prevailing trade in Japan was straightforward: buy stocks, sell bonds. Not anymore.
item.dc:creator: Momoka Yokoyama and Aya Wagatsuma

item.title: Big Take: The Diesel Midterms
item.description: Gas prices are up and Trump is out of time to bring them down before midterms. On today’s Big Take podcast, what high energy prices could cost the Republican party. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Prices Rise Most Since April
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the campaign trail. On today's show, University of Arizona Professor Samara Klar, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Democratic Congressman Don Beyer of Virginia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Army Now Three Years Late Fielding Hypersonic Missile
item.description: The Army said it still hasn’t fully fielded the country’s first hypersonic weapon, acknowledging a more than three-year delay in deploying the advanced technology that has the US lagging China and Russia.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio and Jen Judson
